findings.evidence: At lines 309–314, `hadd` receives only `AEMeasurable g μ` and `hinfty` receives none; the only uses are `hadd g₁ g₂ ...` at line 351 and `hinfty g₂` at line 337, while `g₁` and `g₂` are both indicators of measurable `g` over measurable `S`.
findings.fix: Give `hadd` measurability hypotheses for both `g` and `h`, and give `hinfty` an `AEMeasurable g μ` hypothesis; pass the already-proved measurability of both truncations at the call sites. Apply the same corrected signatures to `lintegral_rpow_operator_le`.
findings.issue: Both public operator theorems require `hadd` for every second input and `hinfty` for every input, including nonmeasurable functions, although the proof uses them only on the measurable truncations `g₁` and `g₂`. This is materially stronger than the usual measurable-input operator laws and makes the advertised reusable interface unusable for such APIs.

summary: The operator API imposes unnecessarily global endpoint laws, preventing use with operators whose standard estimates are stated only for measurable inputs.
